front.title: Proof Closure for Evidence-Bound Effect Protocols

abstract.t: This document describes an Experimental application-layer terminality rule for evidence-bound effect protocols. A system reaches proof closure for one exactly bound subject only when every required proof obligation is satisfied, provenance and verifier bindings are established, a fresh readback has been accepted, declared boundaries are explicit, no obligation remains open, and predecessor evidence has not been transferred to a changed successor.

The rule does not establish the truth of external premises, does not solve the halting problem, and does not create IETF endorsement. It defines a bounded condition for stopping repeated self-verification of an unchanged subject while reopening verification after subject mutation.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Evidence-producing systems can fail in two opposite ways. They can stop while a required obligation remains open, or they can continue producing confirmations after the bound subject is already complete. The first failure is a liveness failure. The second is synthetic progress: additional computation that does not establish a new property of the unchanged subject.
This document defines a bounded proof-closure condition intended for application-layer audit and effect-control protocols. It complements, but does not replace, terminal effect acknowledgement.

section.name: Closure Model
section.t: For an exactly bound subject S, an implementation MAY represent proof closure using the following conjunction:
section.sourcecode: PROOF_CLOSURE(S) = ALL_REQUIRED_PROOFS_VALID(S) and PROVENANCE_BOUND(S) and VERIFIER_CHECKED(S) and FRESH_INDEPENDENT_READBACK(S) and BOUNDARIES_EXPLICIT(S) and NO_OPEN_OBLIGATIONS(S) and SUBJECT_UNCHANGED(S) and NO_PREDECESSOR_EVIDENCE_TRANSFER(S)
section.t: An implementation that claims PROOF_CLOSURE for S MUST be able to identify S unambiguously and MUST bind every required proof and readback to that same subject.
If any required obligation remains open, the implementation MUST NOT claim proof closure.

section.name: Subject Mutation and Successors
section.t: A mutation that changes the bound subject creates a successor subject S'. Closure evidence for S MAY be retained as historical evidence, but MUST NOT by itself establish proof closure for S'.
The successor MUST be rebound and the closure predicate MUST be evaluated against the successor's own required evidence and obligations.

section.name: Relationship to Effect Acknowledgement
section.t: An effect-acknowledgement state and proof closure answer different questions. A terminal effect state indicates completion of one bound effect transition under its protocol rules. Proof closure indicates that no declared proof obligation for the same bound subject remains open.
Neither state is a claim of universal truth. New evidence, a policy change, or a subject mutation can create a new evaluation subject.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Implementations MUST fail closed when subject identity, provenance, verifier identity, freshness, or obligation completeness cannot be established. A boolean assertion of closure supplied by an untrusted producer is not sufficient evidence of closure.
Implementations SHOULD retain predecessor closure receipts for auditability but MUST prevent those receipts from being silently relabeled as successor evidence.

Repeated verification can consume resources and can be abused to create apparent activity. Implementations SHOULD halt repeated closure checks for an unchanged subject unless new admissible evidence, a new obligation, or a changed subject is observed.
